1.definition: Present Simple is used for facts, habits, and permanent situations. Present Continuous is used for actions happening now, temporary situations, and future arrangements.
rules: Use Present Simple for general truths and routines.
Use Present Continuous for actions at the moment of speaking.
Stative verbs (like, know, believe) are generally not used in continuous forms.
1.formula: Present Simple: S + V(s/es). Present Continuous: S + to be + V-ing.
1.timeline: Present Simple: Continuous across time. Present Continuous: Right now.

common_errors.wrong: I am working here since 5 years.
common_errors.correct: I have worked here for 5 years.
common_errors.explanation: Do not use present continuous for actions that started in the past and continue to the present.

examples_interview: Currently, I am leading a team of five engineers (temporary/ongoing).
examples_tech: The system processes 1000 requests per second.
We are migrating the database to AWS this week.
examples_corporate: We are expanding our market presence in Europe.

fill_blanks.q: The compiler _____ (check/is checking) for syntax errors before running the code.
Right now, the server _____ (experiences/is experiencing) heavy load.

error_detection.sentence: I am believing that this is the best approach.

sentence_correction.wrong: He is work as a developer.

2.definition: Past Simple describes completed actions in the past at a specific time. Present Perfect connects the past to the present, focusing on the result or experience without a specific past time.
rules: Use Past Simple with specific time markers (yesterday, last year, in 2020).
Use Present Perfect for experiences, recent changes, or actions with a result in the present.
Never use Present Perfect with a specific past time.
2.formula: Past Simple: S + V-ed/Irregular. Present Perfect: S + have/has + Past Participle.
2.timeline: Past Simple: Specific point in past. Present Perfect: Past action continuing to or affecting present.

common_errors.wrong: I have finished the project yesterday.
common_errors.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a specific past time, so use Past Simple.

examples_interview: I have worked on several microservices architectures (Present Perfect).
examples_tech: We have successfully deployed the new feature.
examples_corporate: The company acquired a startup last year.
Our profits have increased significantly this quarter.

error_detection.sentence: We have launched the product in 2022.

3.definition: Auxiliary verbs used to express ability, possibility, permission, or obligation.
rules: Modals do not take '-s' in the third person.
They are followed by the base form of the verb without 'to'.
Form questions by inverting the modal and subject.
3.formula: Modal + Verb (e.g., can run, must deploy)
3.timeline: Applicable across timeframes, though primarily present/future.

common_errors.explanation: Never use 'to' after a modal verb.

common_errors.wrong: You must to test your code.

examples_interview: You should see an improvement in performance.
examples_tech: The API must handle 10,000 concurrent requests.
We might need to scale the database.
examples_corporate: We should invest more in R&D.

fill_blanks.q: You _____ (must/can) commit your changes before pushing.
We _____ (might/should) delay the launch if the bug isn't fixed.

sentence_correction.wrong: I might to go to the conference.
sentence_correction.correct: I might go to the conference.

4.definition: Used when the focus is on the action or the object receiving the action, rather than who performed it.
rules: Formed with the verb 'to be' + Past Participle.
Use when the actor is unknown, unimportant, or obvious.
Maintains the tense of the active sentence.
4.structure: Object + to be + V3 (+ by Subject)

common_errors.wrong: The code was wrote by John.
common_errors.correct: The code was written by John.
common_errors.explanation: Use the past participle 'written', not the past simple 'wrote'.
The server cannot update itself in this context; it receives the action.

examples_interview: My project was nominated for an award.
The legacy system was entirely replaced.
examples_tech: The data is encrypted before transmission.
The bug was fixed in the latest patch.
examples_corporate: The quarterly report will be published tomorrow.
The decision was made by the board.

fill_blanks.q: The application _____ (is deploying/is being deployed) right now.

error_detection.sentence: The new feature will be release next week.

sentence_correction.wrong: The test run by the QA team.
sentence_correction.correct: The test is run by the QA team.

5.definition: Sentences expressing factual implications, or hypothetical situations and their consequences.
rules: Type 0 (General Truth): If + Present, Present.
Type 1 (Real Future): If + Present, will + Verb.
Type 2 (Unreal Present/Future): If + Past, would + Verb.
5.formula: Type 1: If S+V1, S+will+V1. Type 2: If S+V2, S+would+V1.
5.timeline: Zero: Always. First: Future possibility. Second: Hypothetical present/future.

common_errors.wrong: If I will find a bug, I will fix it.
common_errors.correct: If I find a bug, I will fix it.
common_errors.explanation: Do not use 'will' in the 'if' clause for Type 1 conditionals.

common_errors.wrong: If I am you, I would refactor this.
common_errors.correct: If I were you, I would refactor this.
common_errors.explanation: Use 'were' for all subjects in Type 2 conditional.

examples_interview: If I don't know the answer, I research it (Type 0).
If you hire me, I will bring my AWS expertise to the team (Type 1).
examples_tech: If the server crashes, the load balancer redirects traffic (Type 0).
If we optimize this query, latency will decrease (Type 1).
If we had more memory, the process would be faster (Type 2).
examples_corporate: If profits increase, we will expand (Type 1).
If we changed our strategy, we would see better results (Type 2).

fill_blanks.q: If the test fails, the build _____ (will break/breaks).
If I _____ (have/had) more time, I would write more tests.

error_detection.sentence: If we will launch tomorrow, we will need all hands on deck.

sentence_correction.wrong: If I was the manager, I would approve this.
sentence_correction.correct: If I were the manager, I would approve this.

6.definition: Used to communicate what someone else said, without quoting them directly.
rules: Tenses generally shift back one step into the past (Present -> Past).
Pronouns change to match the perspective of the reporter.
Time and place expressions change (e.g., 'now' -> 'then', 'here' -> 'there').
6.formula: Shift tense back: e.g., 'I am working' -> He said he was working.
6.timeline: Reflects the past statement of a previous action.

common_errors.wrong: He said that he will come.
common_errors.correct: He said that he would come.

common_errors.wrong: She told to me the server is down.
common_errors.correct: She told me the server was down.

examples_interview: My manager said that my code quality was excellent.
They asked if I had experience with Kubernetes.
examples_tech: The QA engineer reported that the tests had failed.
The client stated that they wanted a new feature.
examples_corporate: The CEO announced that the company would merge.
He mentioned that budgets were tight.

fill_blanks.q: He said he _____ (will/would) finish the task by Friday.
She told _____ (to me/me) that the PR was approved.

error_detection.sentence: The lead developer said that the API is working perfectly yesterday.

sentence_correction.wrong: They asked me what is my name.
sentence_correction.correct: They asked me what my name was.

7.definition: Articles modify nouns to indicate specificity. 'The' is definite, 'a/an' are indefinite.
rules: Use 'a/an' for non-specific, singular countable nouns.
Use 'the' for specific nouns known to the listener.
Use no article for plural or uncountable nouns talking generally.
7.formula: A/An + singular countable. The + specific noun.

common_errors.wrong: I am working as software engineer.
common_errors.correct: I am working as a software engineer.

examples_interview: I am looking for a challenging role in a dynamic company.
The project I led increased revenue by 20%.
examples_tech: We need an API gateway to manage the traffic.
The database crashed due to a memory leak.
examples_corporate: The CEO delivered an inspiring speech.
We need a new strategy for the upcoming quarter.

error_detection.sentence: We need to hire an developer.

sentence_correction.wrong: The information are on the website.
sentence_correction.correct: The information is on the website.
